thread:
anya: Heads up — during LingWave v1 int8 onboarding I see a consistent BLEU drop on JA(vertical) and an odd bracket flip in AR-RTL outputs after quantizing. Runs: q5->int8 shadow. Samples attached below. :eyes:

jihoon: Ugh, can you paste the exact eval command & config? Is this only when we enable the new kernel selection path?

anya: Repro steps (short):
```
# run from eval/benchmarks
python eval_multilang.py --model lingwave-v1 --quant int8 --dataset multiorient_sanity --split test --batch 16 --tokenizer-version 2026-03-01
```
Metrics (median over 3 seeds):
- ja-vertical BLEU: baseline (fp16) 28.4 -> int8 23.1 (-5.3)
- ar-rtl sacreBLEU: baseline 31.2 -> int8 29.0 (-2.2) but bracket mirror/ordering errors show up in samples

anya: Example ja-vertical source (short):
"[source with ruby furigana tags and vertical line breaks]"
fp16 pred: "〜漢字（読み）／改行..."
int8 pred: "〜漢字（読み)／改行..."  <-- subtle token join/split at ZWJ + ruby boundary

mateo: Can you dump tokenization diffs? My hunch is token boundary shift with ZWJ/ZWSP near ruby/vertical punctuation interacting with our quantized tokenizer lookup table.

anya: Pasted token diffs (snippet):
```
# fp16 tokens around problem span
['U+3000', '漢字', 'U+200D', '（', '読み', '）']
# int8 tokens
['U+3000漢字', 'U+200D（', '読み', '）']
```

nora: :thinking: interesting. That looks like a tokenmap index shift — maybe the quantized vocab remap (we apply per-shard pruning) collapsed a boundary. Which tokenizer build did you use? The CI onboard uses tokenizer v2026-03-01, but deploy had v2026-03-15 slip?

anya: Confirmed the staging container had tokenizer v2026-03-15 due to image layering. I pinned it to 2026-03-01 and reran — JA BLEU improved by ~1.2 but still behind. So there are two issues: tokenizer drift + runtime kernel difference.

jihoon: For AR bracket mirroring: can you include one minimal example? Also check bidi reordering stage — maybe quant path bypasses our unicode bidi normalization step.

anya: Minimal AR example: source: "(اسم)"
fp16: "(اسم)"
int8: ")اسم("  <-- closing/ opening swapped in the rendered string, orientation reversed inside prediction in some cases

mateo: If bidi reordering is being applied post-detokenize differently, that would explain visual swap. Steps: 1) run raw token sequence compare before detok, 2) compare detok code paths between fp16 and int8 runtime. I suspect a fast-path in the int8 kernel that skips the detok normalizer for perf.

nora: I'll bisect the runtime flags that changed in the quant kernel between changelist 0a7f..1b2c. Assigning to infra:me.

ciara-bot: deploy-checklist: shadow-run created for lingwave-v1:int8 on staging-shadow-04. Link: https://ci.redwood/shadow/3219 :white_check_mark:

jihoon: Action items:
- anya: gather 30 failing samples (JA vertical + AR RTL) and upload to /mnt/triage/lingwave_v1_int8_fails (due EOD)
- mateo: run tokenization diff tool on those samples and attach the deltas (tool: eval/tools/token_diff.py)
- nora: bisect runtime change, check whether detok normalizer was bypassed in quant fast-paths
- infra (cc @infra): ensure tokenizer artifact v2026-03-01 is used for the staging image; prevent auto-latest layering

anya: Uploaded samples here: /mnt/triage/lingwave_v1_int8_fails/3278901234.tar.gz. Quick note: many JA failures have ZWJ+furigana boundaries and linefolding; AR failures concentrated around parentheses, brackets, and Arabic-Indic numerals.

mateo: Ran token_diff on the tarball, summary: 84% of JA fails show token boundary merges around ZWJ/ZWSP; 65% of AR fails show reversed bracket token order pre-detok. Early theory: quantized embedding table pruning + subtoken remap yields different greedy decode steps for identical logits due to rounding. Need to reproduce with deterministic sampling (top-k=1, seed fixed).

jihoon: Good. If deterministic reproduction reproduces flip then it's decoding divergence; if deterministic matches fp16 then it's numerical drift in kernels. Try forcing fp16 kernels with quantized weights (weight-only quant) to isolate.

anya: I ran deterministic top-k=1: divergence still occurs. So it's not sampling nondeterminism. Next test: weight-only quant (keep activations fp16) — results tomorrow morning.

nora: I'll block the int8 rollout until we have root cause. For near-term mitigation, add a post-detok normalizer that re-applies Unicode bidi and bracket mirroring checks for RTL languages on staging responses. That should reduce customer-visible regressions while we debug.

mateo: Also add a tokenization-sanity check in onboarding CI: compare token boundaries against canonical tokenizer artifact and fail the build if >1% mismatch on the smoke set.

anya: Thanks all — attaching a short log excerpt from the failing run for context:
```
[2026-03-22 16:05:12] eval run start: lingwave-v1 int8
[2026-03-22 16:15:34] sample id 42: ja-vertical BLEU drop from 27.9 -> 22.4
[2026-03-22 16:16:01] sample id 84: ar-rtl bracket-order mismatch detected
[2026-03-22 16:20:05] shadow run uploaded to staging-shadow-04
```

nanya: I'll follow up with the weight-only quant results and the 30-sample CSV. :thumbsup:
